units.title: Carrow Point station: fog week, day one.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:30 summary. Pressure 1031 hPa and rising slowly, wind SE 4 km/h, air 6.8 C, dew point 6.4 C, visibility 3 km in mist over the water. That gap between air and dew point is the whole story this week: warm moist air drifting over a cold Sound. Textbook advection fog incoming tonight. The Met Office agrees with me, which is always nice for them.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Thank you for these, they are more use to me than the radio. One small thing, and I say it with affection: it is 'the Met Office agrees with me, which is always nice for it'. An office is singular. I realise nobody minds but me. My washing will go out today regardless and come in damp, as it has since 1971.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Corrected in my head, Mrs Hale. 20:00 summary: air 5.9 C, dew point 5.9 C, saturation. Visibility from my garden is about 60 m; I can't see the lighthouse from the end of the drive, and it's 400 m away. Fog signal started 19:12. Wind calm. If anyone on the coast road wants a number, it's 'slow'.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: From my front room in Gilliver I can see the lamp post outside and nothing past it. The harbour has quite gone. My mother used to say a fog like this was the Sound 'pulling up its blankett'. I have put the kettle on and the lamp in the window and I shall not be going anywhere.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Practical question for the weather man: will it be in Tollinby by the morning school run, and is it the sort that freezes? I have three children, one bus stop and a road with no pavement. I need to know whether to dig out the hi-vis vests they refuse to wear.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Short answer: yes it'll reach you by morning, and no, it shouldn't freeze in Tollinby tomorrow, air stays around 4 C. Brackwater valley is the one to watch for freezing fog later in the week, it pools down there. Dig out the vests. Tell them it's what lighthouse keepers wear. That might work. It didn't on mine.

units.title: Fog delays. Day one. Commentary resumes.
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: 07:30 from Lisle. Twenty minutes late, which Sound Lines calls 'recovering the timetable'. Queue past the newsagent. Visibility fine at Lisle, mist on the water halfway across. Cafe has bacon rolls. We docked at Port Ammet at 08:27, which means I was at my desk at 08:41, which my manager noticed and I noticed him noticing.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: 17:45 return. Departed 18:05. The fog came in properly around Lisle Point, all at once, like someone shutting a door. Engines dropped to a mutter and the horn started. Spent forty minutes looking at a grey window. Arrived 19:02. Tomorrow I'm bringing a book and low expectations.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: It's fog. Boats slow down in fog. That's the whole thread. Some of us drive to work in Tollinby behind a tractor every morning and don't write a diary about it.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Some of us enjoy Ewan's diary very much, and he writes it with a good deal more care than most of what appears on this board. The tractor, I suspect, would not make for such good reading. Ewan, the cafe bacon rolls ran out before Lisle on the way back. I was there.

units.title: Pebble: still looking, now in fog
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Still no Pebble, small grey, one white sock on the front left paw, notch in her right ear. I was out on Tanners Lane and the alleys behind the market with a torch until the fog came in so thick I couldn't see my own feet. I rattled the biscuit box every twenty yards. Two cats came. Neither was Pebble. Both were very pleased with the biscuits.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Moved to Lost & Found, where it will be seen by the people who check it every evening. Please don't worry, it has not been hidden; it is at the top. I would suggest asking the market traders to check their storerooms in the morning. Cats like warm, dry, closed spaces in fog.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Our cat went missing for nine days two winters ago and came back fat and smelling of someone else's fabric conditioner. So that's my hope for Pebble: a second family with a tumble dryer. Have you put her litter tray out by the back door? The smell carries. Sounds gross. Worked for us.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Thank you, TollinbyMum, the litter tray is out, the blanket is out, and I've left the shed door open a crack. Thank you, Mr Pell, sorry for posting in General again. Mrs Ober says her cats are still refusing to go out at all after dark, which she puts down to the fog. I put it down to the fog too.

units.title: Rope Walk recycling. Now moved to Friday. Apparently.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Today's council notice, quoted in full: 'recycling rounds in Rope Walk move from Thursday to Friday for the next three weeks while a vehicle is repaired'. Three weeks. On top of the three weeks already missed. That is six weeks of a recycling box on my step, which by my count will hold eleven milk bottles and the council's own newsletter. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Sympathy from Weyhaven. Our bin store on 8 is full to the door because the residents above 6 have decided the stairwell is haunted and won't carry anything down after dark. I have said it is the lights. I have said it is the lift. Nobody listens to the man on the third floor. Hold firm on Friday, Bernard.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Mr Pryce, a full bin store is a public health matter and I would write to your environmental health officer at once, quoting the relevant waste regulations by section. I have the section numbers if you need them. Whatever your neighbours believe about the stairs is none of our business. The bins are. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.title: Holm boats: busy week at the fuel berth
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Three runs out to the Holm from Gilliver yesterday, two today before the mist came down. Fuel berth's doing well out of it. You can hear the saws from my creel line on a still morning, faint, like a wasp in a jar. Strange hearing it from the Holm side. Nobody's worked over there in my lifetime, nor my father's.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Bram any idea who's running the supply boat? Still after subcontract work on the Holm, chainsaw tickets CS30/31/38, own saws, own PPE, can start tomorrow, no job too small. Heard grieve are paying well but word in the van is you sign on for the lot, no leaving halfway. Fine by me if the money's right.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Aye, it's young Dacre's boat on contract. He'll not take on crew for you, Davey, it's all Grieve's say. I'd leave it, myself. A month on the Holm in the dark end of the year is a long month. That's not gossip, that's just the Holm.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Interesting point about the saws carrying. Over a calm, cold sea sound travels better than people expect: a cool layer of air near the water bends it back down instead of letting it escape upward. Nine kilometres is a long way, but on a still morning with an inversion you could plausibly hear a saw. You certainly hear the Carrow fog signal.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Funny how they started the week the fog came in... Nobody will be watching the Holm for a while now. Not from Gilliver, not from anywhere. I'm not saying it's planned. I'm saying some people check the forecast before they check anything else.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: They started at the start of the month, which is when contracts start. The fog came because it's autumn. Grow up. Some company is cutting down some trees. Next you'll tell us the tide's in on it.

units.title: Brackwater junction lights. Now in fog.
units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: 06:05 Brackwater jct, temp lights on red, no traffic coming the other way, sat there 3 min 40 by the van clock. Council notice now says signals 'are on a fixed cycle and not linked to sensors'. So it's not broken. It's designed. That's worse. Visibility fine this morning, mist on the reservoir. Tomorrow I'll be sat at a red I can't see.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: The school bus driver timed it at four minutes this afternoon. The children have started a sweepstake on how long it'll stay red. My middle one won 20p. I'm told this is educational. Fixed cycle or not, can someone at least put a sign up saying 'yes, you have to wait this long'?

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: 18:20 back through. Red 3 min 55. Fog thick from the reservoir turning onwards, so you're sitting at a red light you can barely make out, in the dark, with a sweepstake running. Tell your middle one I'll take 4 min 10 for tomorrow morning.

units.title: Housekeeping. Kittering Holm threads.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A note for everyone, given the interest in the Holm this week. You are welcome to discuss the clearance. Please do not post the names of individual workers or speculate about named people, and please give a source for any factual claim about the owner or the council. 'Someone told me' is not a source. I will move threads to the right board without comment. Pell.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: With respect Pell, isn't asking for sources a bit convenient when the owner won't release any? Just asking questions. If the council and Ardent Vale won't say what it's for, the only sources are the people asking. Some of us have been doing our research. Watch this space.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Gil, the council has released everything it holds: ADC/VEG/0917, the officer's report, six conditions. It's on the portal. A landowner not announcing a future plan is not the same as hiding a document. If you find a document, post the reference. I'll read it, I promise, and I'll say so if you're right.

units.title: fog notices this week
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: reposting so nobody says they didnt see it. met says fog from 6 tonight for days. coastguard says buoy 3 on the approach is unlit. small boats without radar stay in. if you go out anyway and cant find the entrance dont ring me ring the coastguard. chandlery has reflective tape and spare batteries, normal price, i'm not a pirate

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Hauled the near string at first light while it was only mist. Eleven lobsters, two decent, rest undersized and back over. Leaving the Holm side string till it clears. Price at the quay was down again, the buyer says nobody's driving out to Gilliver in this.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, Rook. To add: buoy 3 failed overnight, I reported it at 07:00. The coastguard work boat will come when it can see what it's doing. Until then please treat the approach as unlit and keep to the leading lights. The slip lights at the foot of the ferry slip are both working again, thanks to the parish lamps. Please don't borrow them.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Engine room view of fog week: radar serviced last month, horn compressor tested this morning, two new lamps in the forward floods. The only thing on board that has ever failed in fog is the people, usually by going out on deck to have a look. Don't have a look. Look at the radar. It's warmer.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Restricted-visibility procedure from this evening on all night runs. Radar watch on the bridge, one lookout forward, sound signal every two minutes, loud-hailer at the wheelhouse door. Kerris has the forward lookout on the late Gilliver leg. If you're meeting the boat at Gilliver, wait at the shelter. Logged, carried on.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Line crew view. Fog's no bother to the poles, it's the salt it leaves behind when it lifts that we pay for in a month. Gilliver feeder was washed in the summer so it should hold. If your lights flicker on the front this week it's more likely the street lighting cables than us. Ring the council for those, not me.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: lookout forward means me freezing at the bow listening for buoys while kerris holds the loud hailer like its a microphone at a wedding. brought two hats and the big flask. if anyone at the gilliver shelter tonight wants to wave that'd be nice, we wont see you but its the thought

units.title: diesel at the berth
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: diesel at the berth gone up 4 cents today. not me, the supplier. reason is half the holm contract boats fill up here now and the tanker cant keep up so its coming round by road. if you need a full tank for the creels get it first thing tomorrow before the contract boat does. dont shoot the messenger lads

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Four cents and the quay price down. Good week to mend creels. Dacre's lad says the island crew order more fuel than food, which is the right way round for saws. He says the landing's terrible at low water and he's had to wade twice. Better him than me.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: The Holm landing beach is shown on the old Admiralty survey as shingle over a rock shelf that dries for nearly 200 m at springs. At neaps, as this weekend, it should be kinder. The surveyors in the 1950s complained about it too. Some things are constant: bad landings, and the price of diesel going one way.
